summary: Kasompe Airport (CGJ) serves Chingola, a major copper mining center in Zambia's Copperbelt Province. The airport supports both civilian and military aviation, having historically hosted elements of the Zambian Air Force. Its location makes it a convenient gateway for mining industry personnel and visitors to the Nchanga copper operations, one of the largest open-pit mines in Africa.
faqs:
Q: Where is Kasompe Airport located?
A: It is located in Chingola, in Zambia's Copperbelt Province, near the DRC border.

Q: Does Kasompe Airport serve commercial passenger flights?
A: It primarily handles charter, private, and mining-related flights rather than scheduled commercial service.

Q: Are there military operations at Kasompe Airport?
A: Yes, the airport has historically hosted Zambian Air Force activity alongside civilian operations.

Q: What is the nearest major city to Kasompe Airport?
A: Chingola itself is the closest town; Kitwe is approximately 35 km away and Solwezi lies to the northwest.
transport_tips: Taxis and private hire vehicles are the most common way to reach the airport from Chingola town center, typically a short 10-15 minute drive. Rental cars can be arranged in advance through operators in the Copperbelt region. Road conditions to the airport are generally paved but can be uneven; allow extra time during the rainy season.
local_tip: Coordinate your arrival with your mining host or employer well in advance, as the airport has limited ground handling services and no scheduled public transport options.
